string-array.name: heart_tips
string-array.item: For adults aged 18 or older, a normal resting heart rate is between 60 and 100 beats per minute, according to the American Heart Association.
Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of death worldwide, taking an estimated 17.9 million lives each year, according to the World Health Organization.
The WHO says most cardiovascular diseases can be prevented by addressing risk factors such as tobacco use, an unhealthy diet, physical inactivity and harmful use of alcohol.
The WHO recommends that adults get at least 150 to 300 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity per week to protect their health, including their heart.
The WHO recommends keeping salt intake below 5 grams per day (about one teaspoon) to help lower blood pressure and the risk of heart disease.
Heart attacks and strokes account for about 85% of all deaths from cardiovascular disease, according to the World Health Organization.
Well-trained athletes can have a resting heart rate as low as 40 beats per minute, which can be perfectly normal for them.
A common estimate of your maximum heart rate is 220 minus your age, according to the American Heart Association.
Your resting heart rate can be raised by stress, caffeine, fever, dehydration, poor sleep and some medications.
For the most representative reading, sit down and rest for a few minutes before measuring your resting heart rate.
Your heart beats about 100,000 times a day, pumping blood to every part of your body.
Regular physical activity strengthens the heart so it can pump more blood with each beat, which often lowers the resting heart rate over time.
World Heart Day is observed every year on 29 September to raise awareness about cardiovascular disease.
